## **Pricing and paywall** {#theme-pricing_paywall}

<!--ir-theme:pricing_paywall-->
   **Pricing and paywall.**
      5 recent review(s) mention pricing and paywall.
      Review window: Aug 8, 2026 - Aug 22, 2026
      **Why it matters:** Users mention price, subscriptions, or paywalls. This can signal pricing sensitivity in the niche.

         **Review examples:**
            1. _valb663_, Aug 22, 2026, 1/5: "zero customer service. wrongfully suspended my trial after 1 day after a studio cancelled on me. worst experience i have ever had and i couldn’t even contact a person to help. Will never be using this platform again, to think i was going to join a monthly plan. Horrible company really."
            2. _yogaforever191_, Aug 19, 2026, 1/5: "I like the concept of classpass and the app is solid. I ended up disliking it because the packages would say "12-22 classes" and would really only get you about 5. Classes are a lot of credits and their estimates are wildly off. Feels deceiving and ends up being more expensive than going through the studio. They need to change their messaging or decrease the cost."
            3. _C.W.2026_, Aug 16, 2026, 1/5: "I’ve used ClassPass consistently and used to genuinely love it. I currently pay $49/month for 23 credits, and there were times when I could take 3–4 classes per week because many of the classes I regularly attended were only 2–4 credits. That has changed drastically. Classes at my regular yoga studio that I historically booked for 2–4 credits are now regularly 4+ credits, and I recently saw a Buti Yoga class listed for 10 credits. That ONE class would use almost half of my entire monthly allowance. ClassPass says pricing fluctuates based on demand, but I’ve attended higher-credit classes that were nowhere near full, which makes the pricing feel arbitrary and incredibly difficult to plan around. What makes this even more frustrating is that the solution ClassPass continually pushes is upgrading to a more expensive plan. But paying more money for additional credits doesn’t solve the underlying problem when the number of credits required per class keeps increasing too. I shouldn’t have to continually increase my monthly spending just to maintain roughly the same fitness routine my existing plan previously allowed. I loved ClassPass because it made fitness more accessible and gave me flexibility. Now the unpredictable credit inflation is actively interfering with the routine I built using the service. Unless the credit system becomes more reasonable and transparent, I’m seriously considering canceling altogether."
<!--/ir-theme-->
